verses.gurmukhi: ਲੋਚਨ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਨ ਅਵਲੋਕਤ ਅਨੂਪ ਰੂਪ ਪਰਮ ਨਿਧਾਨ ਜਾਨਿ ਤ੍ਰਿਪਤਿ ਨ ਆਈ ਹੈ ॥
verses.translit_en: lochan kirapan avalokat anoop roop param nidhaan jaan tirapat na aaiee hai ||

en.bdb: Just as the desire of a miser for money is never satiated, so are the eyes of a Sikh of the Guru who have realised that the form of True Guru is a unique treasure seeing which one never feels satisfied.

verses.gurmukhi: ਸ੍ਰਵਨ ਦਾਰਿਦ੍ਰੀ ਸੁਨਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਬਚਨ ਪ੍ਰਿਯ ਅਚਵਤਿ ਸੁਰਤ ਪਿਆਸ ਨ ਮਿਟਾਈ ਹੈ ॥
verses.translit_en: sravan dhaaridhree sun a(n)mirat bachan piray achavat surat piaas na miTaiee hai ||

en.bdb: Just as hunger of a pauper is never satiated, so are the ears of a Gursikh which are ever desirous of hearing the ambrosial words of the True Guru. And yet hearing those elixir-like words, the thirst of his consciousness is not quenched.

verses.gurmukhi: ਰਸਨਾ ਰਟਤ ਗੁਨ ਗੁਰੂ ਅਗ੍ਰਨੀਵ ਗੂੜ ਚਾਤ੍ਰਿਕ ਜੁਗਤਿ ਗਤਿ ਮਤਿ ਨ ਅਘਾਈ ਹੈ ॥
verses.translit_en: rasanaa raTat gun guroo agraneev gooR chaatirak jugat gat mat na aghaiee hai ||

en.bdb: The tongue of a Gursikh keeps recalling the prime traits of the True Guru and like a rain-bird who keeps shouting for more, it is never satiated.

verses.gurmukhi: ਪੇਖਤ ਸੁਨਤਿ ਸਿਮਰਤਿ ਬਿਸਮਾਦ ਰਸਿ ਰਸਿਕ ਪ੍ਰਗਾਸੁ ਪ੍ਰੇਮ ਤ੍ਰਿਸਨ ਬਢਾਈ ਹੈ ॥੬੨੧॥
verses.translit_en: pekhat sunat simarat bisamaadh ras rasik pragaas prem tirasan baddaiee hai ||621||

en.bdb: The inner self of a Sikh is getting enlightened with blissful light through seeing, hearing and uttering of the wondrous form of True Guru-a treasure-house-nay the fountain-head of all the virtues. Yet the thirst and hunger of such a Gursikh never wanes.  (621)
